sanskrit: अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् । प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया ॥
hindiTranslation: मैं अजन्मा और अविनाशीस्वरूप होते हुए भी तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका ईश्वर होते हुए भी अपनी प्रकृतिको अधीन करके अपनी योगमायासे प्रकट होता हूँ ॥
englishTranslation: Though unborn and imperishable, and though I am the lord of all beings, I manifest myself by controlling my own nature through my own power of appearance.
essence: The unborn can still appear without ceasing to be free.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Krishna says he is unborn and imperishable, yet still appears in the world by using his own power over nature.
simpleInsight: What seems like a birth is really a chosen appearance, not a limitation.
detailedMeaning: Arjuna asked how Krishna could have taught the sun at the beginning of time. Krishna answers that ordinary birth does not bind him at all. With Arjuna confused about time, divinity, and incarnation, Krishna reveals that his appearance is a deliberate manifestation.
modernRelevance: Hearing the Krishna stories from her grandmother at Janmashtami, a child asks how God can be a baby. The grandmother can answer from this verse: the unborn one chooses to appear, by his own power.
translationLiteral: अजः (unborn) / अपि (even though) / सन् (being) / अव्ययात्मा (of imperishable nature) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / ईश्वरः (lord) / अपि (even though) / सन् (being) / प्रकृतिम् (nature) / स्वाम् (own) / अधिष्ठाय (having taken control of) / संभवामि (I manifest) / आत्ममायया (by my own power of appearance)
insight: Unborn and imperishable, Krishna still appears, taking form through his own power over nature.
